question: Can the REST key read a publish schedule back, so `longform monitor` can verify every scheduleId the manifest recorded?
how: A throwaway Go probe (GET only, no credits spent) against https://api.opus.pro with OPUSCLIP_API_KEY from ~/.config/longform-pipeline/env, used only in the Authorization header. Bodies are the real responses scrubbed of the key and of signed URLs; strings longer than 80 characters are cut to keep the file small, and list responses keep their first entries plus the counts. No Authorization header, key or token is stored.

docs.finding: The documented publish-schedules operations are POST (create) and DELETE /{scheduleId} (cancel) only. No GET is documented; the 400 below names two undocumented list modes.

cross_check.tool: claude.ai OpusClip connector, opusclip_list_scheduled_posts (startAt 2026-02-01, endAt 2026-03-01), read-only
cross_check.result: 987 posts: 916 posted, 71 scheduled. Every schedule REST returns for P30122131P0V is status scheduled there; the posted schedules of P30122170hWd.h25EHhZKgK (status posted, post_url set) are absent from REST. The connector carries project_id, clip_id, status (scheduled|posted|failed), post_url and failure_reason; REST carries none of status, post_url or failure_reason.

interpretation.read_endpoint: GET /api/publish-schedules?q=findByProjectAndClip&projectId=P&clipId=C -> 200 {data: [{scheduleId, extUserId, extOrgId, platform, postDetail{title, custom{description, privacy}, thumbnailUrl}, publishAt}]}. clipId is optional (omitted = the whole project). Undocumented; named by the API itself in the 400 for an unknown q.
interpretation.list_endpoint: GET /api/publish-schedules?q=byPage -> 200 {data: {data: [...same entries...], meta: {page, nextPage, total}}}: every pending schedule of the organisation. The cursor semantics are unclear (one call returned all 73 while nextPage was set), so the pipeline does not use it.
interpretation.by_id: GET /api/publish-schedules/{id} does not exist (404 Cannot GET, a route miss, not a missing schedule).
interpretation.semantics: The read endpoints list schedules that are still pending (status scheduled), whatever their publishAt: stale February 2026 schedules that never fired are still listed. A schedule that has posted is no longer listed, and REST has no status, post_url or failure_reason, so it cannot tell posted from failed or cancelled.
interpretation.implication: longform monitor verifies over REST that every OpusClip scheduleId whose publish time is still ahead is pending (findByProjectAndClip once per clip). A scheduleId that is absent after its publish time is recorded as not_pending (left the queue: posted, failed or cancelled; REST cannot tell) and is not counted as verified. Whether a post actually went out is the human check through the connector (opusclip_list_scheduled_posts). Buffer statics are checked against the manifest only.
